recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-37988 unless CQI opens a separate issue for operation-specific error-response guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-37988 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked CQI to correct Measure $evaluate-measure because the out parameter allowed only one MeasureReport even when provider/subject evaluation could produce multiple reports. The adopted resolution changed the return parameter to 0..* Bundle, with one Bundle per input subject and MeasureReport plus evaluated/created-resource content in each Bundle.
initial_application: Historical PR 2305/J#37988 commits 804ded2ef07b29df6025e1a19c572d334c226219 and 060b160cb531b79f1eea1a1b04bf759bd809fc2a applied the change to source/measure/operationdefinition-Measure-evaluate-measure.xml, including changing return from 1..1 MeasureReport to 0..* Bundle. The Measure resource and operation list are active in current build scope through source/fhir.ini and source/measure/list-Measure-operations.xml.
additional_context: The current build retains Measure-evaluate-measure as retired/deprecated and has a successor Measure-evaluate operation. Both now use return min 0, max *, type Bundle. Later related CQI work, especially FHIR-51487 and FHIR-40422, refined the same area of Measure evaluate wording and is already represented on the combined branch. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-37988 found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current operation definitions, response example, and quality-reporting Bundle guidance already convey the resolved Bundle-per-subject behavior and Parameters wrapping for the multi-cardinality return. The original issue's note about OperationOutcome was not part of the final resolution and is covered by the general operations/REST error-response framework rather than by adding OperationOutcome as a success return parameter here.
